crossover.complementarity_analysis: Parent A captures the 30-day range location via the difference between the day index of the 30-day high and the day index of the 30-day low. It measures where the high occurred relative to the low, capturing momentum/mean-reversion timing. Parent B captures the 5-day minimum low relative to current close, a short-term support level. The two signals operate on different time horizons (30d vs 5d) and different aspects (timing of extremes vs price proximity to recent low), providing complementary information. Parent A has a negative orientation, so its value is inverted; parent B is positive orientation.

expected_metric_effects.alpha_diversification: Adds diversity by blending a support factor with a range timing factor
expected_metric_effects.rank_ic_improvement: Expected to improve rank IC by combining independent signals and reducing noise

crossover.integration_logic: The oriented parent A is negated to align with its training direction (-1), converting it to higher-is-better. The oriented parent B is used directly (direction +1). The intermediate factor is the sum of these two oriented signals, allowing both short-term support and intermediate-term range timing to contribute. This additive combination preserves both orientations and captures complementary facets of price action.

factor_spec.description: Intermediate factor combining oriented Alpha158-IMXD30 (negated) and Alpha158-MIN5 via addition
factor_spec.name: G03-CROSS-008-INTERMEDIATE

factor_spec.description: Equal-weight composite of cross-sectional z-scores of Parent A and inverted Parent B. Parent A captures short-term reversal and intraday low/close strength; inverted Parent B captures low crowded price-volume correlation measured over a 60-day window. Higher values are expected to be better.
factor_spec.name: G03-CROSS-001 Oriented Cross Composite (60d Correlation)

mutation.diagnosis: The crossover intermediate blends a short-horizon price reversal component with an inverted medium-horizon price-volume correlation component, each z-scored before an equal-weight add. The blend is sound but a single window change can sharpen the medium-horizon leg without altering the mechanism. The 90-day correlation window is long relative to the weekly rebalance and may be slow to reflect changing crowding regimes. Shortening it to 60 days keeps the same price-volume co-movement construct while making the inverted component more responsive.

expected_metric_effects.mean_rank_ic_20d: Likely modestly higher as the crowding signal reacts faster to regime shifts
expected_metric_effects.monthly_stability: Expected to remain stable or improve slightly due to faster adaptation
expected_metric_effects.rank_icir_20d: May improve from reduced lag in the inverted price-volume component

mutation.mutation_description: Change only the correlation window in the inverted Parent B subtree from 90 to 60 days. All operators, fields, values, min_periods, nesting, and the other leg of the composite are preserved exactly.

mutation.diagnosis: The intermediate blends an oriented price-structure signal with an oriented 90-day price-volume correlation. The medium-horizon Volume leg is the noisier component and its 90-day estimation window may be sluggish for a weekly-rebalanced blend. A single window adjustment on that correlation window tightens the volume component's responsiveness without altering the mechanism or the price leg.

expected_metric_effects.composite_score: Neutral to slightly positive; mechanism and directional orientation unchanged.
expected_metric_effects.mean_rank_ic_20d: Slight improvement expected as the crowding signal responds faster to changes in price-volume co-movement.
expected_metric_effects.monthly_stability: May be modestly more volatile due to shorter estimation window, but should remain comparable.

mutation.mutation_description: Copy the intermediate formula tree exactly and change only the correlation window from 90 to 60, preserving min_periods=1, both operands, the negation, and the equal-weighted add with the price-structure leg.

factor_spec.description: Equal-weighted rank blend of parent A (reversal/low-close strength, with the reversal ts_rank window lengthened to 45) and negated parent B (negative price-volume correlation over 60 days).
factor_spec.name: G03-CROSS-003-MUTATION

mutation.diagnosis: The intermediate equal-weight rank blend of rank(negate(ts_rank(close,30))) plus rank(low/close) plus rank(negate(correlation(return, log(volume ratio+1), 60))) has a short-horizon reversal component (30-day ts_rank) mismatched with a medium-horizon price-volume correlation (60-day). The shorter window is less stable at weekly rebalance and can amplify single-period reversal noise relative to the smoother 60-day volume-correlation leg. Lengthening the ts_rank window from 30 to 45 brings the two legs' lookbacks closer without changing the mechanism, directional sign, ranks, blend, or portfolio rules.

expected_metric_effects.composite_score: Expected to stay comparable or improve slightly via better temporal consistency across the two complementary legs.
expected_metric_effects.mean_rank_ic_20d: Expected to improve modestly by reducing reversal-leg noise from too-frequent resets and better matching the 60-day volume-correlation horizon.
expected_metric_effects.rank_icir_20d: Expected to improve through smoother, more stable cross-sectional ranking of the reversal leg.

mutation.mutation_description: Applied a single window mutation to the copied intermediate formula tree: changed ts_rank(close) window from 30 to 45. Every operator, field, constant, min_periods, ddof, quantile, lag, correlation window, and the final add/rank structure remains identical to the intermediate.

factor_spec.description: Weighted blend of negated Alpha158 CORD120 and RANK10: 0.6 * (-120d close/volume return correlation) + 0.4 * (-10d close rank).
factor_spec.name: G03-CROSS-004 Mutation (120d Correlation Window)

mutation.diagnosis: The intermediate blends a medium-horizon volume-price confirmation term (60d correlation) with a short-horizon price-position term (10d ts_rank). Its main weakness is scale instability: the correlation term is bounded in [-1,1] while the ts_rank term is bounded in [0,1], and both are summed with fixed weights without any cross-sectional calibration, so the blend's dispersion and relative weighting can drift across regimes. A single window mutation that lengthens the slower correlation leg to 120 days aligns the confirmation term more closely with the multi-month horizon where volume-price divergence is more persistent, while leaving the short-term rank leg untouched.

expected_metric_effects.mean_rank_ic_20d: Expected to improve modestly as the longer 120d volume-price correlation reduces noise from short-lived volume spikes and better aligns with persistent divergence signals.
expected_metric_effects.rank_icir_20d: Expected to rise because the slower confirmation leg is more stable across periods, reducing turnover of the blend's signal and improving consistency.
expected_metric_effects.turnover: Expected to decrease slightly as the correlation leg becomes less reactive to temporary volume shocks.

mutation.mutation_description: Change only the correlation window from 60 to 120 days in the first leg of the intermediate; all operators, fields, constants, min_periods, and the 10-day ts_rank window remain unchanged.

factor_spec.description: Window mutation of G03-CROSS-005-INTERMEDIATE: identical combined Parent A plus negated Parent B formula, with the idx_max window changed from 30 to 60 to smooth the extreme-timing signal.
factor_spec.name: G03-CROSS-005-MUTATION

mutation.diagnosis: The intermediate crossover blends a 40-day return-volume correlation signal with a negated 30-day extreme-timing signal. The extreme-timing component relies on idx_max/idx_min over 30 days, which may be unstable because the relative recency measure saturates at window edges. Lengthening that window to 60 days smooths the timing signal and better matches the 40-day horizon of the correlation leg without altering the parent mechanism or operator structure.

expected_metric_effects.composite_score: Expected to remain near the intermediate level with marginal improvement from reduced noise.
expected_metric_effects.mean_rank_ic_20d: Expected to be similar or modestly higher as the extreme-timing leg becomes less noisy at a 60-day lookback.
expected_metric_effects.monthly_stability: Expected to improve slightly due to smoother idx_max timing component.

mutation.mutation_description: Copy the entire intermediate formula tree unchanged and change only the window of the idx_max and idx_min pair... but to keep exactly one window change, change only the single shared alignment window. Since idx_max and idx_min each have window 30 and the divide constant is 30.0, we change exactly one window value (the idx_max window) from 30 to 60 while preserving every other property, op, field, min_periods, constant and argument.

factor_spec.description: Additive blend of two oriented parent signals after a single window mutation: negated 20-day close price rank (changed from 10 days) plus negated 40-day correlation between close-to-close price moves and log volume changes. Both supplied training directions are -1, preserved via root-level negations on each leg.
factor_spec.name: CROSS-RANK20-CORD40-NEGATED-ADD

mutation.diagnosis: The intermediate adds a negated 10-day price-rank momentum leg to a negated 40-day return-volume correlation leg. The price-rank leg is a short-horizon relative-strength measure that can be noisy over a weekly rebalance, while the correlation leg measures whether volume participates in price moves. A single window change on the faster leg from 10 to 20 days lengthens the momentum lookback, reducing turnover-driven noise while retaining the combined parent mechanism.

expected_metric_effects.mean_rank_ic_20d: Expected to remain positive and slightly more stable; a 20-day rank window should better match the 20-day evaluation horizon.
expected_metric_effects.monthly_stability: Expected to remain stable or improve slightly because the longer rank window reduces week-to-week signal churn.
expected_metric_effects.rank_icir_20d: Expected to improve modestly as the faster leg becomes less noisy while the volume-confirmation leg remains unchanged.

mutation.mutation_description: Change the ts_rank window on the close price-rank subtree from 10 to 20 days. Copy the rest of the intermediate formula tree exactly, preserving both negate ops, the add root, the correlation window of 40, all min_periods, constants, and argument structure.

mutation.diagnosis: The intermediate factor sums two oriented, complementary signals: a negated 40-day return-volume correlation (flow/participation confirmation) and a negated 5-day stochastic range position (short-term price extremity). The two windows (40 and 5) are mismatched, so the short-term range component can be noisy relative to the medium-term correlation anchor. Widening the stochastic window from 5 to 10 days smooths the price-position leg, reducing turnover-driven noise while retaining the combined mechanism.

expected_metric_effects.mean_rank_ic_20d: Slight improvement expected from a less noisy short-term position leg that aligns better with weekly rebalancing.
expected_metric_effects.rank_icir_20d: Expected to increase modestly due to reduced turnover and noise in the price-extremity component.

mutation.diagnosis: The intermediate factor adds two oriented signals: negated 30-day IMXD timing and 5-day MIN5 support proximity. Its weaker component may be the very short 5-day rolling minimum, which is noisy and dominated by recent micro-moves rather than stable support. Lengthening that window slightly should reduce noise in the support leg while preserving the combined additive mechanism and the 30-day timing leg.

expected_metric_effects.rank_ic_improvement: Smoother short-term support leg reduces noise, modestly improving rank IC stability
expected_metric_effects.turnover_reduction: Longer support window lowers churn in the MIN5 component
